diviner-gcp.citation: Williams, J.-P., Paige, D.A., Greenhagen, B.T., Sefton-Nash, E. (2017), The global surface temperatures of the Moon as measured by the Diviner Lunar Radiometer Experiment, Icarus 283, 300-325, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2016.08.012
diviner-gcp.license: CC0-1.0 (NASA-led mission data archived by the NASA Planetary Data System; no restrictive notice on the product page)
diviner-gcp.native_resolution: 0.5 x 0.5 degree (up to ~55 km in latitude near the pole)
diviner-gcp.nodata: -9999.0 (documented no-observation constant); negative radiance values also occur
diviner-gcp.notes: Coarse context only. This is not the 240 m PCP product and is never mixed with the committed PCP window values.
diviner-gcp.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node / UCLA Diviner Lunar Radiometer Experiment
diviner-gcp.qa: fill constant and physical range checked per row; no interpolation
diviner-gcp.uncertainty: no per-cell uncertainty column; the table reports brightness temperatures and bolometric brightness temperatures from cumulative nadir observations

diviner-prp.citation: Paige, D.A., et al. (2010), Diviner Lunar Radiometer Observations of Cold Traps in the Moon's South Polar Region, Science 330, 479-482, doi:10.1126/science.1187726; LRO Diviner Polar Resource Product V2.0, PDS4 label dlre_prp_south.xml
diviner-prp.depth_support: temp_avg at 2 cm below the surface; temp_max at the surface; ice_depth is a modeled sublimation-stability depth
diviner-prp.license: CC0-1.0 (NASA-led mission data archived by the NASA Planetary Data System; no restrictive notice on the product page)
diviner-prp.local_time_support: annual average and annual maximum, not a local-time sample
diviner-prp.native_resolution: 2,880,000-triangle mesh covering a square centred on the south pole to 80 S; triangle edge length is approximately 0.3-0.4 km. The product does not publish a single nominal resolution.
diviner-prp.nodata: ice_depth -999.0 means the modeled depth exceeds 2.8738 m
diviner-prp.notes: Model-derived. ice_depth is the depth at which water ice would sublimate at 1 kg m-2 per billion years; 0 means stable at the surface. It is not an observed ice detection, ice fraction or mineable-ice estimate.
diviner-prp.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node / UCLA Diviner Lunar Radiometer Experiment
diviner-prp.qa: temperature range and depth range checked per triangle; physical zero retained
diviner-prp.temporal_support: no observation start/stop in the label; annual quantities derived from Diviner climatology and a Kaguya DEM
diviner-prp.uncertainty: no per-triangle uncertainty in the product; modeled quantities, not measurements
diviner-prp.version: LRO-L-DLRE-5-PRP-V2.0, PDS4 product version 1.0, calibration software 4.0

odyssey-ns.citation: Feldman, W.C., et al. (2002), Global Distribution of Neutrons from Mars: Results from Mars Odyssey, Science 297, 75-78, doi:10.1126/science.1073541; PDS Geosciences Node Odyssey GRS special product ns_epithermal_020917
odyssey-ns.license: CC0-1.0 (NASA-led mission data archived by the NASA Planetary Data System; no restrictive notice on the product page)
odyssey-ns.native_resolution: 0.5 x 0.5 degree (about 29.6 km at the equator)
odyssey-ns.nodata: no fill constant is documented; non-positive cells are treated as no_coverage and are never interpreted as physical zero
odyssey-ns.notes: Counts/second, not the normalized HEND epithermal flux ratio. The two products use different instruments and normalization and are not comparable.
odyssey-ns.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node / 2001 Mars Odyssey Gamma Ray Spectrometer
odyssey-ns.qa: finite and positive check; no interpolation
odyssey-ns.temporal_support: first 25.7 days of Odyssey mapping (2002); exact start/stop not stated in the label
odyssey-ns.uncertainty: no per-cell uncertainty column in the ASCII table

tes-timap.citation: Putzig, N.E., Mellon, M.T., Heet, T.L., Ward, J.G. (2009), MGS Mars TES Derived Thermal Inertia Maps V1.0, MGS-M-TES-5-TIMAP-V1.0, NASA PDS; Putzig and Mellon (2007), Icarus 191, 68-94, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2007.05.013
tes-timap.depth_support: upper few centimetres (apparent thermal inertia retrieval)
tes-timap.license: CC0-1.0 (NASA-led mission data archived by the NASA Planetary Data System; no restrictive notice on the product page)
tes-timap.local_time_support: dayside and nightside maps, no single local solar time
tes-timap.native_crs: Mars planetocentric simple cylindrical, R=3396.0 km, positive east
tes-timap.nodata: interpolation mask 0 marks infilled pixels; values outside 5-5000 rejected
tes-timap.notes: Coarse context only. TES TIMAP uses a different retrieval, support and method version from the committed THEMIS 100 m product; the two are never mixed.
tes-timap.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node / MGS TES / Southwest Research Institute
tes-timap.qa: mask applied per pixel; only non-interpolated native pixels are reported
tes-timap.temporal_support: TES observations Feb 1999-Apr 2004, three Mars years; day and night maps; no per-pixel acquisition time is carried by the map
tes-timap.uncertainty: no per-pixel uncertainty layer; the data set cites Putzig and Mellon (2007) for retrieval accuracy and provides a separate interpolation mask

notes: Full source metadata for the new sources. Reused #43/#44 observations are linked by observation_id in aoi_evidence.json and are not rewritten.
